speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. You have reported increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months; can you tell me if this pain occurs while you are resting or only during activity?

Also, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a visible deformity in the knee, and does the swelling improve after applying ice or elevation?

Finally, do you have a history of gout, rheumatoid arthritis, or any recent knee injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter disease (though atypical for age 24 without trauma history, consider Sinding-Larsen-Johansson or synovial chondromatosis).

REQUEST TEST: X-ray of left knee (AP, lateral, and sunrise views).
REQUEST IMAGES: Left_knee_mri.

Please confirm if you have noticed a lump or bony prominence just below the kneecap or at the top of your shin, and if you are an athlete involved in jumping or running sports.
